title: Locality contracts and staged fallback for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Customers who purchase regional dedicated pools need both throughput guarantees and clear data residency enforcement, but current placement and failover rules either violate residency constraints during load spikes or cause large latency/capacity penalties when honoring strict zone affinities. Goals: (1) Provide stable locality contracts that guarantee a minimum throughput band in-region, (2) implement a staged, observable fallback that preserves residency where possible and degrades gracefully when necessary, (3) integrate with autoscaler policies to pre-warm capacity without violating residency locks, and (4) minimize KV cache cold-start impact during spillovers. Proposed design: 1) Locality contract tokens - each Dedicated reservation exposes a set of locality tokens representing guaranteed throughput capacity per region/zone (e.g., 100 tps @ region-west-1). Tokens are consumed by assignment logic and replenished on reservation scaling events. 2) Residency lock levels - three lock levels: HARD (never cross-region), SOFT (prefer in-region, allow spill after grace window), and FLEX (best-effort but attempt local placement). 3) Staged fallback sequence: PREFER_LOCAL -> SOFT-SPILL (route to nearby zone with cached prefix affinity) -> QUANTIZED-FALLBACK (serve with smaller/quantized model variant in-region) -> CROSS-REGION-EMERGENCY (last-resort, audited and rate-limited). 4) Autoscaler policy changes: predictive pre-warm triggers based on 5m q95 traffic forecasts to allocate locality tokens and provision warm KV cache shards. Pre-warm respects HARD locks (no cross-region pre-warm) and for SOFT locks will pre-warm both primary and one secondary zone. 5) KV cache migration: implement a lightweight prefix shadowing mechanism to copy hot prefixes to secondary shards during the SOFT-SPILL window to reduce token cache misses. 6) Observability and SLA mapping: surface locality token utilization, spill counts, and per-contract degradation stage in Console dashboards and alerting. Trade-offs: increased scheduling complexity; additional bookkeeping for tokens and cache shadowing; small resource overcommit during pre-warm; slightly longer scheduler latency to evaluate staged fallback policies. Acceptance criteria and non-goals are listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Contraction/expansion of locality tokens is visible in Console and matches Dedicated reservation changes
Under controlled load test, a HARD-locked reservation never routes outside its residency region
SOFT-locked reservations only cross-region after configured grace window and emit an audit event
End-to-end median tail latency increase during SOFT-SPILL remains <= 15% and p95 <= 2x compared to steady-state local serving
KV cache miss rate during staged fallback reduced by >= 40% vs no shadowing baseline
Autoscaler pre-warm triggers at 5m q95 should achieve >= 90% successful pre-bound placements without violating HARD locks
All fallbacks produce an auditable event with reason, chosen fallback stage, and affected contract id
testing_plan: Unit tests for locality token lifecycle and lock enforcement
Integration test harness simulating cross-zone outage and validating staged fallback sequence
Chaos run: induce 20% zone capacity loss in a canary region and measure spill metrics and client-visible latency
Load test with synthetic traffic patterns (burst, steady, diurnal) to validate autoscaler pre-warm and token consumption
End-to-end QA with a seeded customer reservation in test org and manual verification of audit logs and console metrics
rollout_plan: Prototype scheduler plugin behind feature flag for 5% of internal Dedicated capacity (week 1)
Enable SOFT lock behavior for non-production reservations and validate metrics (week 2)
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% for SOFT lock path over 4 weeks with automated canary checks
HARD locks gated behind security review; enable for customers on request after audits (post-week 4)
Monitoring: add SLOs for spill rate and token utilization; automatic rollback on >10% of contracts entering CROSS-REGION-EMERGENCY
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Token bookkeeping bug could double-allocate throughput. Mitigation: conservative allocation and quorum-based token updates with immediate circuit-breaker and rollback
Risk: Pre-warm increases cloud costs. Mitigation: estimate cost delta and expose per-reservation pre-warm budget; default to conservative thresholds
Risk: KV shadowing increases memory pressure. Mitigation: bounded shadow cache size and LRU eviction prioritized for non-critical prefixes
Risk: Auditing volume spike. Mitigation: sample audit events and provide high-fidelity dumps for incidents only
